Lauren — thanks for the note and the redline. I had a quick pass and highlighted the practical/legal levers we should use: 

1) Keep uncapped carve-outs limited to fraud and willful misconduct. We should be firm that fraud and intentional wrongdoing are uncapped, but we can insist on the usual proofs (clear and convincing standard) for fraud.

2) Gross negligence is a broad and risky term; if ACME insists we can offer a narrowed formulation — e.g., "gross negligence that is the proximate cause of material direct damages resulting from a breach of a material obligation" — and limit evidentiary threshold (preponderance of evidence). Alternatively, swap to "reckless disregard" for a higher scienter bar.

3) Monetary threshold / floor: propose an exception to the cap for gross-negligence-level claims where damages exceed the greater of $250,000 or 0.5% of the trailing 12-month fees paid under the Order Form. This lets us keep predictability while giving recourse for meaningful harms.

4) Regulatory fines / statutory penalties: where liability arises from Redwood's willful violation of applicable law (e.g., data privacy statutes), we should agree to cooperate on remediation and make space for recovery of direct losses and reasonable investigatory costs, but push back on unlimited consequential damages. Consider a carve-out for statutory penalties only to the extent they are finally adjudicated against Redwood for willful misconduct.

5) Contract drafting: provide ACME with two short options — (A) our preferred (cap remains, explicit willful/fraud uncapped, gross negligence limited and subject to monetary floor) and (B) a middle ground (gross negligence carved out up to 2x fees but with a $250k floor). Let them pick.

I'll draft the two options and a short covering note. If Marissa/AE want to soft-sell option B to preserve the deal, fine; we should keep A as baseline.

-David Kim

Emily — thanks for the redline. Attached is our response with two compromise options, as discussed with our legal team. Short summary below: 

• Willful misconduct/fraud: uncapped (Redwood accepts uncapped liability for proven intentional misconduct and fraud, subject to clear-and-convincing proof).
• Gross negligence: Redwood prefers to limit/exclude from uncapped treatment. Our preferred position (Option A) narrows the term to "gross negligence constituting a proximate cause of material direct damages resulting from a breach of a material obligation" and makes an exception only where such damages exceed the greater of $250,000 or 0.5% of trailing 12-month fees.
• Option B (commercial compromise): carve-out for gross negligence up to 2x fees paid under the Order Form, with a $250,000 floor.
• Regulatory fines: we will accept liability for statutory fines only where finally adjudicated for Redwood's willful violation of law; we propose a cooperation and mitigation clause for data incidents.

Please see Redwood_MSA_response_v1.docx and let me know which option they prefer; happy to hop on a short call with you and Tom to move this along.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
